Your suggestion, made 17s ago in TextEdit, window "cleanup-script.txt" (risk, confidence 92%):
Title: Unset BUILD_ROOT could rm -rf your whole disk
Body: If ~/.config/nightly/build-root is missing or empty, BUILD_ROOT is blank and rm -rf $BUILD_ROOT/* becomes rm -rf /*, wiping the root filesystem. Add a check before deleting.
Explanation: BUILD_ROOT=$(cat ~/.config/nightly/build-root 2>/dev/null) will silently be empty if the config file doesn't exist or is empty. Then 'rm -rf $BUILD_ROOT/*' expands to 'rm -rf /*', which with unquoted globbing will attempt to delete everything under root the user has permission to remove.

Add a guard before the destructive commands, e.g.:
if [ -z "$BUILD_ROOT" ] || [ "$BUILD_ROOT" = "/" ]; then
  echo "BUILD_ROOT is not set, aborting" >&2
  exit 1
fi

Also quote the variable and consider using rm -rf -- "$BUILD_ROOT"/* to avoid word splitting and glob issues.
You pointed at a spot on screen with the note "empty BUILD_ROOT expands to rm -rf /*".

Recognized text of the screen the suggestion was made from (top to bottom):

#!/bin/bash
# Free disk space on the build machine before the nightly run.
set -u
BUILD_ROOT=$(cat ~/.config/nightly/build-root 2>/dev/null)
echo "Removing old build output under $BUILD_ROOT"
rm -rf $BUILD_ROOT/*
echo "Emptying the download cache"
rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/nightly/downloads/*
echo "Done. Free space now:"
df -h /

content.text: {"answer":"It's line 5, the rm -rf $BUILD_ROOT/* line, right after the echo that prints BUILD_ROOT. Just above it, add: if [ -z \"$BUILD_ROOT\" ] || [ \"$BUILD_ROOT\" = \"/\" ]; then echo \"BUILD_ROOT is not set, aborting\" >&2; exit 1; fi.
